text: Ascaris, Toxocara, red worms, Taenia, and Coccidiosis are common internal parasites. Scavenging animals, free-range flocks, and free-grazing cattle are more vulnerable because they easily ingest eggs and larvae shed on the ground. Impacts include: nutrient loss and poor body condition from worms absorbing essential nutrients; death in severe cases (e.g. Toxocara can kill young buffaloes and cattle); organ damage (liver, intestine, lungs) causing diarrhea and coughing; and zoonotic risk, since some internal parasites (e.g. Taenia, Trichinella) can transmit to humans.
